title: Introduce async-prefetch rotary-aware attention kernel with hybrid-striping and adaptive KV cache gating
author: Ava Kim
description:
Context: Production chat and short-sequence workloads show high per-token overhead from attention kernel dispatch and excessive KV cache churn when multiple low-latency requests are interleaved. This PR introduces a new rotary-aware attention kernel that performs asynchronous prefetching of Q/K/V tiles and a hybrid-striping scheduler that balances warp-level striping with bank-coalesced micro-tiles. In addition, an adaptive KV cache gating mechanism is added to reduce memory thrash for streaming workloads.

What this PR does (high level): - Adds a new CUDA kernel (async_prefetch_attn) that prefetches rotated KV prefixes asynchronously while computing QK product, avoiding a strict blocking fetch for common rotary/rope layouts. The kernel is rotary-aware (computes sin/cos transforms fused into the prefetch path). - Implements a hybrid-striping scheduler that chooses between warp-striping and micro-tile striping based on sequence length distribution and batch shape heuristics. This reduces bank conflicts on medium-short sequences (<=512) while preserving throughput on long sequences. - Adds adaptive KV cache gating: a runtime policy that decides when to materialize KV entries for in-flight contexts vs. reference-prefetch-only paths to reduce memory pressure on multi-session streaming. - Introduces scheduler hooks and config knobs (hybrid_striping_mode, async_prefetch_enable, kv_cache_gating_threshold) exposed through the runtime config API and Redwood Console. - Adds microbenchmarks, unit and integration tests, and documentation for the new kernel and knobs.

Motivation: Teams running interactive assistants and streaming pipelines saw tail-latency amplification when many short requests shared GPU pools. The combination of prefetch stalls and KV cache churn was the primary contributor. This change targets those hotspots with an optimized kernel and a smarter scheduling policy.

Compatibility and rollout: The kernel is guarded behind a runtime feature flag (async_prefetch_enable=false by default for private installs). For hosted/dedicated we enabled it in canary pools with automatic fallback to the existing flashbridge kernel when the new kernel fails or when CUDA capability/driver versions are unsupported. The PR also includes runtime detection for CUDA >= 11.8 and a safe fallback path.

Benchmarks: See performance_summary field for a short summary. Full benchmark scripts are in tests/bench.

Notes: The description contains implementation rationale and a short checklist. See release_notes for user-visible items.
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial async prefetch kernel, scheduler integration, KV gating policy, tests and benchmarks, docs and feature-flag wiring, CI fixes for GPU matrix multiply edge-case.
review_comments: Diego Ruiz: Overall nice work, the microbench harness is convincing. Requested: please add an assertion for CUDA compute capability at kernel launch to avoid miscompiles on older drivers.
Author (Ava): Added capability guard and unit test in tests/unit/test_kernel_capability.py, pushed in commit 4/6.
Priya Nambiar: Can we avoid materializing sin/cos tables per-thread? Suggest sharing per-block precomputed tables for common rotary dims; this will reduce register pressure.
Author (Ava): Implemented block-shared sin/cos cache with fallback to per-thread compute for rare dims; updated microbench to measure register usage impact.
Ethan Zhao: Approve after CI green. Noted a small formatting nit in hybrid_striping config docs; resolved.
Release lead (comment): Please ensure canary rollout is coordinated with SRE; added post-merge job to kick off canary validation.
SRE (comment): Canary on dedicated pools shows no OOMs after 48h; metrics look good.
QA (comment): Regression test failed on a precision edge-case (fp16 accumulation disabled). The PR includes a fallback that disables async-prefetch for that config; added test citing the behavior.
performance_summary: Microbenchmarks (A100, fp16 accumulation enabled, continuous batching on): median latency down 10-18% for sequences <=64, p95 down 8-12%; end-to-end throughput +12-16% for 4-8 concurrent streams. For long sequences (>1024) no measurable degradation; hybrid-striping defaults to long-path. KV gating reduced working set memory by ~22% on chat-heavy traces, lowering OOM and eviction rates in canary runs.
release_notes: Add rotary-aware async-prefetch attention kernel (opt-in initially)
Introduce hybrid-striping scheduler with runtime knob hybrid_striping_mode
Adaptive KV cache gating to reduce memory churn on streaming workloads
Expose feature flags: async_prefetch_enable, kv_cache_gating_threshold; default off for private installs
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge into main by release-bot. All reviewers approved. Post-merge: canary rollout started for dedicated pools; automated canary validation job passed after 48h. No rollbacks required.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. Kernel is feature-flag guarded and includes defensive fallbacks (CUDA capability check and a software fallback path). Requires CUDA >= 11.8 for best performance; runtime will disable on unsupported hosts. Regression tests added to cover precision and fallback paths.
testing_notes: Integration: end-to-end streaming smoke with continuous batching enabled
Benchmarks: tests/bench/short_seq_bench.py, bench scripts in docs/perf run_bench.sh
Canary: dedicated-pool canary for 48h with traffic replay
